body:
`.github/workflows/tests.yml:183` — *"Comment PR with results"*, `actions/github-script@v9`,
`if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && failure()`. It calls `github.rest.issues.createComment`,
and the job's token lacks `pull-requests: write`, so **the step itself fails**:

    failure  .github:31     Unhandled error: HttpError: Resource not accessible by integration
                            https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#create-an-issue-comment
    failure  .github:16751  Process completed with exit code 1.

**OBSERVED 2026-08-30 on PR #2053, job 99285787916.**

## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

The step only runs `if: failure()` — so it fires **exactly when a human is trying to read why CI is
red**, and it adds a top-line annotation that names an authentication problem instead of the test.
Neither annotation names the failing test. The real cause was
`test_findings_ledger.py::test_committed_index_matches_a_regeneration_from_the_real_items`.

Compounding it: **job logs are unavailable while any other job in the run is still going**
(`run … is still in progress; logs will be available when it is complete`), so during the window
where the annotations are the only evidence, the only evidence is misleading. The reliable move is
to run the suspect test locally.

So the step's net effect today is **negative**: it never delivers the comment it exists for, and it
degrades the diagnosis it was meant to improve.

## Two options — this needs a decision, not a default

1. **Grant `pull-requests: write`** to the fast-tests job. Delivers the intended comment.
   ⚠️ This repo is deliberate about workflow scopes — `tests/unit/test_auto_revert_confirms_before_reverting.py::test_confirmation_does_not_widen_workflow_permissions`
   exists specifically to stop permissions creeping. Widening one should be an explicit choice, and
   the narrowest form is a separate job with only that permission, not a wider fast-tests token.
2. **Delete the step.** The rollup and annotations already tell a reader the job failed; the comment
   adds a duplicate channel that has never worked. Costs nothing and removes the misleading output.

Option 2 is the smaller change and loses nothing that currently works. Option 1 is only worth it if
someone actually wants the comment.
title: CI's failure-only PR comment step lacks pull-requests: write, so it throws over the real test failure
